long_biography.plain_text:
An existing Manhattan hotel gave Vikram Chatwal the opportunity to test a different approach to hospitality. His father, Sant Singh Chatwal, offered him a tourist-class property, which he transformed into The Time. Its design-led approach provided the basis for a broader collection within the family’s hotel business.

At Dream Downtown, Chatwal commissioned Handel Architects to rework an unusual wedge-shaped building. The renovation placed a glass-bottomed swimming pool above the lobby and created a beach-like courtyard. Restaurants and nightlife were central to the project: partnerships with specialist operators helped attract local New Yorkers as well as overnight guests.
